file-abort.description: Remove the part a copy to a path left on this machine.

params.name: path
params.description: The file the copy was for. An absolute path, or one that starts with ~.

params.name: part_id
params.description: The copy's part id, up to 32 hex digits: the part is .NAME.tuios-part-ID, so two copies to one path write two parts. Omit for .NAME.tuios-part.

returns.name: path
returns.description: The path.

file-commit.description: Finish a copy written with open-file-stream: check the part's sha256 against the sender's, then rename it into place. A part that does not match is removed.

params.name: path
params.description: The file the copy is for. An absolute path, or one that starts with ~.

params.name: sha256
params.description: The sender's hash, hex. Omit to skip the check.

params.name: conflict
params.description: When the path exists: replace it, keep both (the copy gets a new name), skip (the part is removed and the file there stays), or fail.

params.name: label
params.description: keep-both names the copy "name (LABEL).ext", such as "report (from build).pdf". Omit to name it "name 2.ext".

params.name: perm
params.description: The original's permission bits, which the finished file gets. Omit to keep it owner only.

params.name: mtime
params.description: The original's modification time, Unix ms, which the finished file gets. Omit to keep the time of the copy.

params.name: part_id
params.description: The copy's part id, up to 32 hex digits: the part is .NAME.tuios-part-ID, so two copies to one path write two parts. Omit for .NAME.tuios-part.

returns.name: path
returns.description: Where the file is now.

returns.name: sha256
returns.description: The part's hash.

returns.name: skipped
returns.description: conflict skip found a file at path, so the copy was removed and the file there stays.

file-hash.description: The sha256 of a file on this machine, of a range of it, or of the part a copy to it is writing.

params.name: path
params.description: The file. An absolute path, or one that starts with ~.

params.name: offset
params.description: Where the range starts.

params.name: length
params.description: How many bytes. Omit for the rest of the file.

params.name: part
params.description: Hash the part file of a copy to this path.

params.name: part_id
params.description: The copy's part id, up to 32 hex digits: the part is .NAME.tuios-part-ID, so two copies to one path write two parts. Omit for .NAME.tuios-part.

returns.name: sha256
returns.description: The hash, hex.

returns.name: bytes
returns.description: How many bytes were hashed.

file-list.description: List a folder on this machine a page at a time, folders first, then names in natural order (file2 before file10), with size, time and mode.

params.name: dir
params.description: The folder. Omit for the home folder.

params.name: offset
params.description: The first entry of the page.

params.name: limit
params.description: Entries in the page, at most 5000.

params.name: hidden
params.description: Include names that start with a dot.

returns.name: dir
returns.description: The folder, made absolute.

returns.name: entries
returns.description: One info object per entry, as file-stat's info.

returns.name: total
returns.description: Entries in the folder.

returns.name: next
returns.description: The offset of the next page. Absent on the last page.

returns.name: parent
returns.description: The folder above. Absent at the root.

returns.name: home
returns.description: This machine's home folder.

returns.name: capped
returns.description: The folder holds more than 50000 names, and only those were read.

returns.name: access
returns.description: Over a link only: what the linked machine may do in the folder. files says the link allows files, write that the machine may write here, and roots the folders it may write in.

returns.name: denied
returns.description: Over a link only: how many names the read deny list leaves out.

file-mkdir.description: Make a folder on this machine, with its parents.

params.name: path
params.description: The folder. An absolute path, or one that starts with ~.

params.name: receive
params.description: Make the receive folder instead, and ignore path: where a copy from the caller lands when it names no folder. For a linked machine it is the first folder of its files_roots, else ~/Downloads/tuios.

returns.name: path
returns.description: The folder, made absolute.

file-read.description: Read up to 4 MiB of a file on this machine, base64.

params.name: path
params.description: The file. An absolute path, or one that starts with ~.

params.name: offset
params.description: Where to start.

params.name: length
params.description: How many bytes, at most 4 MiB.

returns.name: content
returns.description: The bytes, base64.

returns.name: size
returns.description: The file's size.

returns.name: eof
returns.description: The read reached the end of the file.

file-remove.description: Delete a path on this machine. A folder that holds files needs recursive. The home folder and / are refused.

params.name: path
params.description: The path. An absolute path, or one that starts with ~.

params.name: recursive
params.description: Delete a folder and all it holds.

returns.name: path
returns.description: The path deleted.

file-rename.description: Move or rename a path on this machine. It does not replace a path that is there unless replace is set. A move to another disk answers cross_device: copy it with transfer-start and move set.

params.name: from
params.description: The path to move.

params.name: to
params.description: The new path.

params.name: replace
params.description: Replace what is at to.

returns.name: from
returns.description: The old path.

returns.name: to
returns.description: The new path.

file-stat.description: Describe one path on this machine. With part, describe the part file a copy to the path is writing. With names, describe up to 256 names in the folder path.

params.name: path
params.description: The path. An absolute path, or one that starts with ~.

params.name: part
params.description: Describe the part file of a copy to this path instead.

params.name: part_id
params.description: The copy's part id, up to 32 hex digits: the part is .NAME.tuios-part-ID, so two copies to one path write two parts. Omit for .NAME.tuios-part.

params.name: relation_to
params.description: Another path on this machine. The reply says how path stands to it, with links followed.

params.name: names
params.description: Names in the folder path, at most 256. The reply has infos for them in place of exists, size and info.

returns.name: path
returns.description: The path, made absolute.

returns.name: exists
returns.description: False when nothing is there.

returns.name: size
returns.description: The size in bytes. 0 for a part that is not there.

returns.name: info
returns.description: name, path, kind (file, dir, symlink, other), link_kind and link for a link, size, mtime (Unix ms), mode (drwxr-xr-x), perm (the permission bits as a number), hidden.

returns.name: relation
returns.description: With relation_to: same when the two paths are one file, inside when path is in the folder relation_to, apart otherwise.

returns.name: infos
returns.description: With names: an info for each name that is there and that you may read, in the order of names.

file-walk.description: List every file and folder under a folder on this machine, for a folder copy. At most 20000 entries in one reply; with stream, up to 1000000 entries, one JSON line each after the reply, and a last line {end, bytes, skipped, skipped_count, denied} or {end, code, error}. Links are not followed: a link, a named pipe, a socket and a device are not copied, and skipped names them. Over a link, an entry in the read deny list is left out and not named, and denied counts it.

params.name: path
params.description: The folder. An absolute path, or one that starts with ~.

params.name: stream
params.description: Send the entries after the reply, one JSON line each, for a folder of more than 20000 entries.

returns.name: entries
returns.description: rel (the path under the folder, slash separated), size, dir, perm, mtime (Unix ms). A folder comes before what it holds.

returns.name: bytes
returns.description: The bytes of every file together.

returns.name: skipped
returns.description: The first 200 items a copy does not carry: rel and kind (symlink, pipe, socket, device).

returns.name: skipped_count
returns.description: How many items a copy does not carry, all of them.

returns.name: denied
returns.description: Over a link, how many entries were left out because a linked machine may not read them. A folder counts once. They are not named.

open-file-stream.description: Turn this connection into the bytes of one file. mode read: after the reply the connection carries the file from offset to size, then closes. mode write: the part file beside path is cut to offset, then the connection takes length bytes into it, answers one line {part_size, written, error} and closes. file-commit puts the part in place.

params.name: path
params.description: The file to read, or the file a write is for. An absolute path, or one that starts with ~.

params.name: mode
params.description: read or write.

params.name: offset
params.description: Where the bytes start. A write's offset cannot be past the part's end.

params.name: length
params.description: write only: how many bytes the caller sends.

params.name: part_id
params.description: The copy's part id, up to 32 hex digits: the part is .NAME.tuios-part-ID, so two copies to one path write two parts. Omit for .NAME.tuios-part.

params.name: sum
params.description: read: after the last byte, one line {sha256} with the hash of the bytes sent, or {error} when the file changed while it was read.

params.name: progress
params.description: write: while the bytes land, one line {written} at most every 250 ms with the bytes written so far, before the last line.

params.name: compress
params.description: read: "auto" lets this machine compress the bytes with flate when a sample of the file compresses well, and the reply says compressed. write: true when the caller sends the bytes as one flate stream.

returns.name: size
returns.description: read: the file's size. The connection carries size minus offset bytes.

returns.name: mtime
returns.description: read: the file's modification time, Unix ms.

returns.name: compressed
returns.description: read: the bytes come as one flate stream.

returns.name: sum
returns.description: read: a {sha256} line follows the bytes.

returns.name: part_size
returns.description: write: the part's size before it was cut to offset.

file-trash.description: Move paths to the trash of this machine. A linked machine may trash only paths it may write. A path that fails does not stop the rest.

params.name: paths
params.description: The paths.

returns.name: trashed
returns.description: One object per path the trash took: from, the path it was at; file, the path in the trash; info, the trash info file.

returns.name: error
returns.description: Why a path was left, when one was.

file-untrash.description: Put a file the trash took back where it was. The trash must have taken it from to, and to must be free.

params.name: file
params.description: The path in the trash, as file-trash answered it.

params.name: to
params.description: The path it came from.

returns.name: path
returns.description: The path it is at now.
